findings.summary: `manifest.sceneLightMeshLists` was an unconditional key, so the branch added it to all 221 scene manifests while `reachFeature("light:included-meshes")` already answered the same question three lines away; the field, its private, its manifest write and its member are gone and compose-pipeline reads the feature list, restoring manifest byte-identity with main for every scene the branch cannot reach

`gltfLightmapMaterials` was a second copy of `gltfRenderables`' node-major/primitive-minor traversal, in the same file and already diverged — it read `primitive.material` raw where the original resolves it through `variantMaterialIndex`, so a container with a selected `KHR_materials_variants` would have been stamped against the unmapped index; `gltfRenderables` now carries the pinned renderable name and the lightmap walk filters its result

`staticStringList` duplicated `Compiler.staticStringElements` and disagreed with it — the copy could not see a `const` array binding nothing writes through; the pure probe is now on `AssignmentContext` and answers first, with the value-carried fallback kept for an inlined helper's argument

`writesThroughArray` re-implemented `writesThroughRoot`'s three write clauses and disagreed about an unrecognized method; `writesThroughRoot` gained a `mutatesVia` predicate so a caller that knows its value is an array passes the exact `mutatingArrayMethods` set while the shared default stays conservative, and the array scan keeps only the argument-escape clause that is genuinely its own

`callParameterIsReadOnly` duplicated the nested-call signature resolution inside `parameterIsReadOnly`, and the copy lacked its `storingDataMethods` skip; extracted as `callArgumentIsReadOnly` and both read it

`assertNoSecondSelector` re-implemented `bindsEnclosingLoop` more weakly — it did not stop at a nested loop, a nested function-like or a nested switch, so a `for` or `switch` inside a lightmap walk body refused where the sibling container walk correctly allows it; extracted as `enclosingLoopControl`, which returns the offending statement so a caller can refuse at it, with `returns` as the lightmap walk's extra clause
the torus-knot helper's tuple-return hook re-derived `lowerTupleComponents`, which the splat lowerer already calls inside exactly this `std::array` wrapper; the hook now calls it

`pinnedMeshOptionLocals` added a second `??`-head recognizer to the module that already owns one, and the two disagreed: `pinnedDefaultExpression` takes the outermost `??` of the left spine (so `diameterTop ?? diameter ?? 1` is an option defaulting to 1) while the new reader required the `??` to be the initializer and its left to be the bare option read, omitting `diameterTop` entirely; the new reader now walks the same left spine

the continuation nesting re-indented everything already nested inside it at every level, making emitted whitespace quadratic in the number of frame boundaries — 115 KB at 160, 92% of it leading spaces; indentation now stops past eight levels, which is linear and moves no byte for any registered scene (the deepest is six)

`scenePbrSetters()` was awaited unconditionally in `materialSubjects`, three lines under the comment documenting that module's deferral discipline, resolving eight more pinned modules for a stamp both of whose call sites are guarded — measured 8.5 ms per glTF scene, ~0.64 s across a corpus compile since each scene is its own process; now deferred behind the lightmap guard

`isParseFloatCallee` took a five-line identical arrow at all three call sites and `"parseFloat"` remained in the identifier array the helper now decides; the helper takes the context and the dead array entry is gone

the lightmap walk's filter detection was a triple-nested ternary that forced an `as ts.IfStatement` cast to read back what it had just narrowed, and its function-boundary test spelled out four `ts.isFunctionDeclaration`-style checks; narrowed once and kept, cast deleted, four-way test replaced by `ts.isFunctionLike`
`containsEntryEngineOperation` looped over a two-element name array around a doubled identifier/property test; the callee name is read once and compared

the texture UV-property write guarded `field.value === "boolean"` and then re-tested `property === "invertY"` inside it, though `invertY` is the only boolean in `TEXTURE_UV_PROPERTIES` — which is why the refusal beside it can name that property; the outer test now states the condition, and the doubled `compileBoolean` of the same expression is compiled once and reused by the record store
the lightmap selection type was written inline three times in one file plus once in compose-pipeline; named `SceneLightmapSelection` once

the torus-knot capture assertion tested each captured name against the intersection it had just derived rather than against the option list it means; stated against the options, with the intersection taken after

the MSVC nesting ceiling behind the frame-yield unroll: `C1061: compiler limit: blocks nested too deeply` at 43 nested lambdas (bisected, 42 compiles), where the development default clang-cl accepts 320 and shipping builds use MSVC
findings.blockedBy: The fix is a counted re-queue (`defer_start_continuation_after`) collapsing a run of adjacent EMPTY continuation parts, which re-pins the module digests of scenes 129 and 271 — both already emit adjacent empty parts — so it needs its own golden recapture rather than riding this branch. No registered scene comes near the ceiling: the deepest continuation any of them emits is six levels, and scenes 113/114/115/118 emit nine. The quadratic-whitespace half of the same finding IS applied.

findings.summary: `containsFrameYield` is OR-ed into `requiresStaticIteration` at one of that predicate's call sites, so the budgeted-uniform arm and the `for-of` arm still answer the pre-change question
findings.blockedBy: Extending it widens what the budgeted-uniform arm and the `for-of` arm accept, turning loops that currently refuse into unrolled ones. Nothing has measured what those two sites would then lower, and no reached scene puts a frame yield through either, so there is no case to measure against yet.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, 'Closures and async' — recorded on the continuation-collapse entry, which is the same mechanism and the same pass

findings.summary: the lightmap walk mints its own licence by climbing `node.parent` to an enclosing `for-of`, where this repository mints the equivalent proof on the loop BINDING (`Value.assetWholeMeshList`, set by `emitAssetFlattenedMeshesForOf` and read by `setPbrUnlit`), so the two setters accept different walk shapes and neither accepts the other's
findings.blockedBy: Unifying them means minting a licence at `emitHandleCollectionForOf` via its existing `extraBinding` hook and moving BOTH setters onto it, which widens what each accepts — `setPbrLightmap` would gain `getContainerMeshes` walks and `setPbrUnlit` would gain `scene.meshes` walks. That is a capability change with its own gates, not a refactor. The contained half of the finding — the duplicated break/continue policy — is applied above via `enclosingLoopControl`.
findings.filedIn: docs/features.md, the PBR lightmap paragraph — states that the two loaded-material stamps reach their walks differently, what each therefore refuses, and what unifying them would take
